# Manifest Format

<!-- GENERATED by scripts/generate-authoring-reference-docs.ts. Do not edit the reference sections by hand. -->

Spellkave bundles are TOML manifests loaded by the CLI and admitted by the
`r_apply_world_manifest` reducer. The row/field reference below is generated
from `spellkave_schema::manifest_json_schema()`.

## Required Header

```toml
#:schema https://spellkave.dev/schema/world-manifest-1.0.0.json
schema_version = "1.0.0"
```

## Applyset (root manifests)

A root manifest names the applyset it belongs to with one top-level field,
right after the header (ADR-0145):

```toml
applyset = "srd"
```

Every applyset apply (`r_apply_bundle`, which `sk dev seed`/`sk dev up` use)
refuses a root without it; the server's applyset memory is keyed by this name,
not by `bundle_id`. Only the root declares it: an `[[include]]` fragment
that sets `applyset` is rejected. The other apply reducers ignore the field.

`sk diff -k` displays file changes, world-added rows on pruned entities with `--prune`, and
**authored, changed in the world since the last apply**. Existing readable rows absent from
memory are `adopt`: they gain memory without a live upsert. Changed file
rows compare live values with the last sealed comparable hash; adoption
compares live values with the files. Conflicts stop `sk apply -k` before it
sends (exit `2`); `--force` makes the files win and updates the baseline.
Unchanged drifting rows remain informational. Unavailable export, unsupported
row kinds, unread live placement and missing comparable hashes produce
explicit `not_checked` reasons, never an assertion of no drift.

## Initial Capability Extents

An `entity_definition_initial_capability` row has optional
`extent_kind_ref` and `extent_ref` strings. Both default to empty.
They describe the scope that a newly realized instance must retain; they
must not be silently dropped when applying or spawning the definition.

Manifest commit and definition seeding preserve both strings on the realized
capability row. Empty extents retain their existing behavior.

### [[entity_definition_equip_modifier]]

Schema row: `EntityDefinitionEquipModifierRow`.

sk-ct8.3 / finding #37 (BL-19): "item is in a slot" → modifier fold on the WEARER. Each row says "while an entity of `entity_def_id` sits in ANY of the wearer's `entity_equipment_slot` rows, fold `modifier_template_id` into the wearer's effective-int overlay." Read at fact-collection time by `entity_facts.rs`'s equipped-item fold — NOT a spawn-time seed like its `entity_definition_initial_*` siblings.

| Field | Required | Type |
|---|---:|---|
| `bundle_id` | yes | `string` |
| `entity_def_id` | yes | `string` |
| `modifier_template_id` | yes | `string` |
